title: Electronic origin of ion-specific structural responses: The role of charge density and self-interaction error
title_zh: 离子特异性结构响应的电子起源：电荷密度和自相互作用误差的作用
summary: 从头算分子动力学为水系统提供了第一原理框架，但其准确性受到交换相关泛函中的自相互作用误差 (SIE) 的限制。虽然已知 SIE 校正可以减少散装水中的过度结构化氢键，但它们对离子水合的影响仍不清楚。
abstract: Ab initio molecular dynamics provides a first-principles framework for aqueous systems but is limited in accuracy by self-interaction error (SIE) in exchange-correlation functionals. While SIE corrections are known to reduce the over-structured hydrogen bonding in bulk water, their impact on ion hydration remains unclear. Here, we employ machine learning molecular dynamics to systematically compare the Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof functional with Tkatchenko–Scheffler–van der Waals dispersion correction and the strongly constrained and appropriately normed (SCAN) functional, thereby investigating the effects of different treatments of exchange-correlation (including SIE) on the hydration structure and electronic properties of Na + and Cl − in aqueous solutions. We find that the SCAN functional yields a more ordered and compact first hydration shell of Na + , while leaving the orientational distribution of water molecules largely unchanged. In contrast, for Cl − , the Cl–water correlation of the first hydration shell remains nearly unchanged, whereas the orientational distribution of surrounding water molecules is significantly modified. Charge density analysis reveals that these differences originate from ion-dependent electronic responses: the charge density is more localized around Na + under the SCAN description, strengthening Na + –water interactions, whereas Cl − is comparatively less affected. These results reveal that ion-specific hydration responses are governed by electronic structure effects, particularly charge-density differences associated with reduced SIE, and highlight the importance of accurate treatment of electronic structure in aqueous simulations.

title: Influence of Deposition Conditions on Ferroelectric, Piezoelectric, and Leakage Characteristics in Cobalt-Doped CaBi₄Ti₄O₁₅ Thin Films Prepared using Pulsed Laser Deposition
title_zh: 沉积条件对脉冲激光沉积钴掺杂CaBi₄Ti₄O₁₅薄膜铁电、压电和漏电特性的影响
summary: 无铅 Aurivilius 铁电材料由于其优异的热稳定性和环境兼容性，在高温压电器件、非易失性存储器和能量收集应用中引起了极大的兴趣。在这些材料中，CaBi4Ti4O15（CBT）表现出有前景的铁电性能；然而，其功能性能受到沉积条件和缺陷化学的强烈影响。
abstract: Lead-free Aurivillius ferroelectric materials have attracted considerable interest for high-temperature piezoelectric devices, non-volatile memories, and energy harvesting applications owing to their excellent thermal stability and environmental compatibility. Among these materials, CaBi₄Ti₄O₁₅ (CBT) exhibits promising ferroelectric properties; however, its functional performance is strongly influenced by deposition conditions and defect chemistry. In this study, 4 mol% cobalt-doped CaBi₄Ti₄O₁₅ (CBT-Co) thin films were deposited on Pt(111)/Ti/SiO₂/Si substrates by pulsed laser deposition (PLD) to investigate the influence of substrate temperature (600 and 700°C) and oxygen partial pressure (0.01, 0.05, and 0.10 mbar) on their structural, morphological, ferroelectric, piezoelectric, and electrical properties. The deposited films were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), atomic force microscopy (AFM), piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM), polarization–electric field (P–E) hysteresis measurements, and current–voltage (I–V) analysis. The results demonstrate that deposition conditions significantly affect crystallinity, grain morphology, domain switching behavior, leakage current, and piezoelectric response. The film deposited at 600°C and 0.10 mbar exhibited the best overall ferroelectric performance, showing a remanent polarization of 6.17 µC cm⁻² and a coercive field of 148.8 kV cm⁻¹ at an applied voltage of 20 V, together with well-developed ferroelectric domains and improved polarization switching. In contrast, films deposited at higher substrate temperature exhibited larger coercive fields, indicating stronger domain pinning associated with microstructural evolution and oxygen-vacancy-related defects. The optimized deposition conditions also resulted in reduced leakage current and enhanced effective piezoelectric response, confirming the strong correlation between processing parameters and functional properties. These findings demonstrate that careful control of substrate temperature and oxygen partial pressure is crucial for tailoring the microstructure and enhancing the ferroelectric and piezoelectric performance of Co-doped CBT thin films. The present study provides valuable insights into the processing–structure–property relationships of Aurivillius thin films and offers an effective strategy for developing lead-free ferroelectric materials for advanced electronic and electromechanical applications.

Here, the authors use neutron diffraction to show that the example of NbFe 2 provides the first case, where the masking modulated order is a longitudinal spin-density wave. The latter has a large-wavelength incommensurate modulation of its low average moment and is formed from ferrimagnetic building blocks with antiparallel ferromagnetic sheets.
